summaryBox.title: Ether Chemistry Rules
summaryBox.takeaway: Williamson: Alkyl halide MUST be 1° or Methyl. 3° halide gives E2 alkene. HI Cleavage: 1°/2° = S_N2 (I⁻ on smaller group); 3° = S_N1 (I⁻ on 3° group); Anisole = Phenol + CH₃I.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
WILLIAMSON SUBSTRATE CONSTRAINT
                       
   Target: Synthesis of *tert*-Butyl Methyl Ether [$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-O-CH}_3$]
   
   PATHWAY A (Correct):   $\text{CH}_3\text{Br } (1^\circ) + (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-O}^-\text{Na}^+ \xrightarrow{S_N2} \mathbf{(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-O-CH}_3} + \text{NaBr}$
   
   PATHWAY B (Incorrect): $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-Br } (3^\circ) + \text{CH}_3\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+ \xrightarrow{E2} \mathbf{(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2 \text{ (2-Methylpropene)}} + \text{MeOH}
   
   *RULE:* The alkyl halide MUST be $1^\circ$ or Methyl. A $3^\circ$ halide acts via $E2$ elimination!
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Williamson Synthesis**: $\text{R-X} + \text{R'O}^-\text{Na}^+ \to \text{R-O-R'} + \text{NaX}$. Halide must be $1^\circ$; $3^\circ$ halides give E2 alkene elimination.
- **HI Cleavage Kinetics**:
  1. $\text{CH}_3\text{-O-CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HI} \xrightarrow{S_N2} \mathbf{\text{CH}_3\text{I}} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
  2. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-O-CH}_3 + \text{HI} \xrightarrow{S_N1} \mathbf{(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-I}} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$
  3. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-O-CH}_3 \text{ (Anisole)} + \text{HI} \longrightarrow \mathbf{\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH \text{ (Phenol)}}} + \mathbf{\text{CH}_3\text{I}}$

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
10 NEST ALCOHOLS, PHENOLS & ETHERS TRAPS SUMMARY

1. Anisole + HI produces Phenol and Methyl Iodide (NOT iodobenzene and methanol).
2. t-Butyl bromide + sodium methoxide yields 2-methylpropene via E2 (NOT ether).
3. Lucas test: 3° immediate, 1° needs heat.
4. Phenol (pKa ~10) is 10⁶x more acidic than ethanol (pKa ~16).
5. Reimer-Tiemann uses neutral dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂), NOT a carbocation.
6. Methanol poisoning is treated by intravenous ethanol (competitive inhibitor).
7. Bromine water + phenol yields a white ppt of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.
8. Victor Meyer: 1° = Red, 2° = Blue, 3° = Colorless.
9. Ethanol at 413 K gives Diethyl ether; at 443 K gives Ethene.
10. PCC stops 1° alcohol oxidation at Aldehyde (stopping over-oxidation).
